title: Arithmetic Operators
objectives: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulus.
theory: Arithmetic operators act on numeric values. The plus operator + adds, minus - subtracts, asterisk * multiplies, forward slash / divides, and percent % computes the remainder.
When both operands are int, division produces an int result truncating any fractional part. (int)7 / 3 is 2. When either operand is double, division produces a double. 7.0 / 3 is 2.333...
The modulus operator returns the remainder. 17 % 5 is 2 because 17 divided by 5 is 3 with remainder 2. Modulus helps detect even and odd numbers: number % 2 == 0 means even.
Order of operations follows the PEMDAS/BODMAS rule: parentheses first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right.
Expressions commonly represent real calculations. A game might compute damage as baseDamage * multiplier - armourReduction.
terms: The order in which operators execute.
tryIt: Calculate a recipe scaling, a game score penalty, and a remainder from a division.
challenge: Write a calculation for employee overtime pay, student average marks, and enemy health reduction.
summary: Arithmetic operators calculate new values. Division behaves differently for int and double. Modulus finds remainders. Order of operations governs evaluation.
quiz: One double operand produces a double result.
The remainder of 17 divided by 5 is 2.
